deities: Hanuman (as guardian of Ayodhya, holding infant Ram in his lap)

history.dynasty: Reconstructed during the Nawab of Awadh era (land revenue granted 1855; built by Tikait Rai)
history.period: Ancient site (shrine attributed to Maharaja Vikramaditya's era; present structure 19th century)
history.summary: Hilltop fort-temple dedicated to Hanuman, guardian of Ayodhya. Tradition holds an ancient shrine was erected by Maharaja Vikramaditya; after its destruction the site was known as Hanuman Teela, and the present Hanuman Garhi was built during the Nawab era by Tikait Rai (the Nawab of Awadh granted land revenue in 1855). The Bairagi Mahants of the Ramanandi Sampradaya and Nirvani Akhara have charge of the shrine. The main idol shows Hanuman in the Anjaneyudu form, seated peacefully cradling the infant Ram in his lap inside a cave shrine, a depiction unusual in north India. The temple is reached by 76 stone steps, has four corner bastions like a fort (garhi), and pilgrims traditionally visit here before Ram Janmabhoomi, seeking Hanuman's permission. OPENING-HOURS CONFLICT: sources variously list 4:00 AM-1:00 PM/3:30 PM-9:00 PM, 5:00 AM-12:00 PM/4:00 PM-9:00 PM, or 5:00 AM-10:00 PM continuous (verify locally).

name: Hanuman Garhi
town_description: Ayodhya is an ancient city on the Saryu river in Uttar Pradesh, one of the seven most sacred pilgrimage cities (Sapta Puri) of Hinduism and, by tradition, the capital of the Kosala kingdom and birthplace of Rama. Renamed from Faizabad in 2018, it is now a major pilgrimage destination with its own international airport and has become one of the most visited religious sites in the world.

travel.airport: Maharshi Valmiki International Airport, Ayodhya (~15 km); Lucknow Airport (~135 km)
travel.railway: Ayodhya Dham Junction (~1 km; the temple is a walkable distance from the station)
travel.road: ~1.6 km from Ram Janmabhoomi; buses run from Lucknow and Agra; cabs/autos available in the city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Tuesdays and Saturdays see special crowds; allow 30-45 minutes here before walking to Ram Mandir.
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT: published timings vary - common listings are morning 5:00 AM-12:00 PM and evening 4:00 PM-9:00 PM (some say 4:00 AM-1:00 PM / 3:30 PM-9:00 PM; some say 5:00 AM-10:00 PM with a brief midday bhog closure). Entry is free. Footwear must be removed at the base of the steps; photography allowed.
